item.title: Why Cincinnati Bengals' Zac Taylor should be on hotseat | Williams
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals struggled for three seasons to win down-to-the-wire games. The defense couldn't hold the dam. Fans begged for change. The front office finally overhauled the defense last offseason. The Bengals pulled out a 43-36 overtime win against the lowly Tennessee Titans before a mostly subdued 66,209 fans at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1, aided by a couple of key defensive stops down the stretch, including a sack by the biggest offseason acquisition. Quarterback Joe Burrow, guarding his words, made sure to point out in his mixed-emotions presser: "We lost that game the last three years." The Bengals are 5-2. Who Dey, baby! They're rolling, right? Not exactly. The excitement is tempered. Something seems amiss about this team, despite the Bengals being off to their best start through seven games since the 2021 Super Bowl season. This team expected to play championship football. Burrow said so during training camp, and fans bought in. But the Bengals have fallen well short of playing like a Super Bowl contender so far. It took overtime to beat the one-win Titans, who traded away their best defensive player last week. It begs the question: Did the Bengals change enough? All eyes are on coach Zac Taylor, in his eighth season in Cincinnati. He's an offensive guru, but his offense is stale and predictable and really hasn't change much, if at all, since his team caught the NFL by surprise in that 2021 season. Should Taylor be on the hotseat? Absolutely. Quietly, Taylor probably has been on the hotseat since the start of the season. The Bengals haven't been to the playoffs since 2022. The front office invested $125 million in three veteran defensive free agents and traded for Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence , whose sack with 32 seconds left in regulation ensured the game would be extended. The Bengals brought back all their starters on offense. Most have assumed a deep playoff run is the minimum expectation of this team or else it should be time for a coaching change. Frankly, this team looks like a one-and-done wild-card team at best right now. And there's simply no indication the Bengals are going to suddenly transform from a middling team into a championship-caliber club. The Bengals keep running the same game plan on offense week in and week out. They keep starting slow. They refuse to consistently run the ball. The Bengals still can't line up inside the 10-yard line and run over teams. They keep operating mostly out of the shotgun, telegraphing that Burrow is either going to pass the ball to Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins. Same scheme, different season. The Bengals committed four turnovers and got buried in a 13-0 hole out of the gate for the second consecutive week. Last week in Baltimore, Burrow turned it on in the second half. This week, Burrow turned it on in the last two drives of regulation and in OT. There has been no semblance of consistency. Of the four Diamondbacks nominated for Gold Gloves in the National League, three of them were winners. Gabriel Moreno won at catcher, Geraldo Perdomo at shortstop, and Corbin Carroll in right field. The only Arizona nominee not to win, was Ildemaro Vargas who was one of the final three in the utility category. That went to Mauricio Dubón of Braves (he was a sort of incumbent, having won the American League award there last year, as an Astro). Perdomo and Carroll won their first Gold Gloves, while it was Moreno’s second honor, having previously taken it home in 2023. The three awards ties a franchise record. The Diamondbacks also won three in 2019, courtesy of Nick Ahmed (SS), Zack Greinke (P) and David Peralta (OF). Corbin Carroll, right field Despite experiencing a relatively down year offensively at the plate, hitting .239 with 22 hkme-runs, Carroll leaned heavily into his elite speed and defensive instincts to anchor the right side of the outfield at Chase Field. Carroll led all MLB right fielders with +10 Outs Above Average (OAA), Defensive Runs Saved (DRS) largely agrees, scoring him +12 there, ranking him second in the NL. His win is particularly impressive, considering his reputation for a relatively weak arm. But the highlight reel below shows, that isn’t necessarily the case. The Dallas Cowboys ’ disappointing collapse against the Arizona Cardinals was not enough to shake owner Jerry Jones’ confidence in head coach Brian Schottenheimer . Instead, Jones publicly acknowledged that several people had let the head coach down during the game, while Schottenheimer also had a strong response ready when asked about his owner’s comments. During his postgame press conference, the head coach accepted his accountability for the disappointing performance while also saying that the Cowboys had made several costly mistakes across all three phases of the game. “I’ll always own my part of this, as the head football coach,” Schottenheimer said. “You know, it starts with me and there’s certainly things that I need to do better. But as a football team in all three phases, I can point out 3, 4, 5, 6 plays right off the top of my head but I’m not going to do that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott also openly voiced his support for the head coach . Meanwhile, Jones made it clear after the game that he was not contemplating any coaching changes. That means the head coach seemingly still has an opportunity to turn things around. However, Schottenheimer also made it clear that he wasn’t going to dwell on the disappointment. “I’m disappointed,” he added. “But I only know how to do it one way, and that’s to work. I’m a worker. I’m a problem solver.”’ “I think we’ve got guys in that locker room that are problem solvers. We have guys in there that want to be great. As a leader, I’m gonna stand in front and hit them with the truth.” The magnitude of Dallas’ collapse becomes even more astonishing considering the franchise’s historical record in similar situations. item.title: ‘I’m gonna fix that’- Tom Brady breaks apology promise with second live-TV slip-up
item.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images Tom Brady has found himself in trouble again after appearing to swear during FOX’s NFL Sunday pregame show, despite previously apologising for his language and promising to clean it up. The seven-time Super Bowl champion made the slip during a trivia segment about career passing records, reacting after incorrectly answering a question alongside Drew Brees and the studio crew. Brady is still adjusting to life as a broadcaster after 23 seasons in the NFL, with his latest mistake bringing renewed attention to his on-air language. Tom Brady makes another slip after promising to clean up his language During the segment, Brady was asked about quarterbacks with the most career games recording at least 300 passing yards. Brees topped the list with 123, followed by Brady with 113 and Peyton Manning with 93. Brady mistakenly named Brees when asked who ranked third, then blurted out: “Oh S***!” The reaction drew laughter from the FOX studio, but it also marked another slip for the former quarterback after he had already addressed his language earlier in the season. During FOX’s coverage of the Dallas Cowboys’ game against the Washington Commanders in Week 2, Brady reacted to a replay of Jayden Daniels dislocating his left elbow. “ Oh S****,” Brady said before adding: “Excuse me. I was not expecting to see that.” He also used another profane expression while analysing a 35-yard completion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb during the same game. Brady later addressed the incidents in his #AskTom segment for NFL on FOX, admitting that his language had crossed a line. “I’m actually kind of embarrassed. There’s a lot of grandmas at home that probably aren’t very happy with my mouth on Fox. I’m gonna fix that. Sorry. I apologize,” he said. His latest slip has also raised questions about the rules governing profanity on broadcast television. Federal restrictions apply to obscene, indecent and profane content, particularly during daytime hours, although not every swear word automatically constitutes a violation. There is no confirmed investigation or penalty involving FOX over Brady’s latest remark. Brady has previously made similar slips during broadcasts, including an apparent interrupted expletive while discussing Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts in 2025. His latest mistake suggests that keeping his language in check remains a challenge as he continues his broadcasting career. item.title: How Notre Dame’s opponents fared in WEEK 9 of the CFB season
item.description: PROVO, UTAH - OCTOBER 31: Jayven Williams #15 of the BYU Cougars defends Omarion Miller #4 of the Arizona State Sun Devils against the pass during the second half at LaVell Edwards Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Provo, Utah. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Notre Dame’s 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but “tough” or anywhere near the word “hard” was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media). Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Against Navy, Notre Dame took a slower path than fans would like, but in the end the Irish won the game 35-13 and completely shutdown the Middies in the 2nd half. Next up for the Irish is the No.1 ranked Miami Hurricanes in a prime time matchup in South Bend. Notre Dame is still likely to be favored in every game this season, and they are still a popular pick to win the national championship. Their strength of schedule probably isn’t going to matter much, but let’s keep track of it anyway. In a strong rookie class, Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg is making the case that he is the best of the bunch. The start of Lendeborg's season has been tremendous, sliding right into the Warriors rotation. In fact, Lendeborg is already one of the Warriors' best and most important players next to franchise legend Steph Curry. With Curry out on Sunday against the Los Angeles Clippers , the Warriors needed someone to step up and take control of the offense. Lendeborg was up for the challenge, scoring points at a rate that no Warriors rookie has done since Curry himself. If Lendeborg can keep this up, he radically changes the expectations for the Warriors this season and in the future, with the rest of the roster aging. item.title: 'I'm going to do': Paul George says there's only one thing he cares about right now with the Boston Celtics
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Paul George is having a fine debut season with the Boston Celtics. The veteran was traded to the Celtics by the Philadelphia 76ers, who swapped him for Jaylen Brown. That move has worked out really well for both teams. George has averaged over 20 points per game so far this season, but he has now claimed that he doesn’t care about scoring anymore. Instead, his full focus is on his biggest objective. Paul George says he only cares about winning the NBA Championship with the Boston Celtics George is in his 17th year in the NBA, having started his career with the Indiana Pacers in the 2010-11 season. The now-36-year-old has always been highly regarded, but despite his longevity, he has never even come close to winning an NBA Championship Ring. George wants to change that now after helping the Boston Celtics go 5-1 this season, with their most recent win coming against the Orlando Magic on Sunday night. The veteran made it clear in an interview after the game that he no longer cares about scoring points or amassing individual statistics. All he is interested in now is winning the championship. He told NBC Sports Boston: “At this point in my career, year 17, that’s all I care about. I don’t care about scoring. I don’t care about whatever it is. It’s all about winning. “I’m going to do whatever I can to win, leave it all on the floor for these guys, give ourselves a chance to win. That’s all that matters. I’ve done it all, I’ve seen it all, I’ve been there and done that. I’m yet to win. That’s the one thing I’m seeking.” The Celtics are definitely not the favourites to go all the way from the East. Many people think it will be George’s old team, the 76ers, who will do it. However, with Jayson Tatum firing and George himself impressing, they could surprise people and go the distance if they keep improving in the coming months. item.title: Patrick Mahomes’ Wife Brittany Calls Out Refs After Chiefs-Broncos Game
item.description: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes' wife, Brittany Mahomes, sounds off on the refs' final call against the Broncos. Getty Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes throws against the Broncos at Mile High Stadium. Getty The Kansas City Chiefs fell to the Denver Broncos in dramatic fashion on Sunday, November 1. After blowing an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, they lost 28-24. On fourth-and-one, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid chose to let Harrison Butker attempt a 54-yard field goal instead of going for it with 2:36 left in regulation. However, Butker missed wide right, giving the Broncos excellent field position to march down the field and take the lead. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes appeared to throw a game-winning touchdown to wide receiver Rashee Rice as the clock expired, but it was called back due to a holding penalty on Jaylon Moore. To say Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, was upset may be an understatement. Patrick Mahomes’ Wife, Brittany Mahomes, Sounds Off on the Refs’ Final Call Getty Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes throws against the Broncos at Mile High Stadium. After the game ended, Brittany did not hold back her thoughts. She posted on her Instagram Stories, “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can’t tell me otherwise.” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid appeared to be on the same page. Speaking to reporters about that final penalty, “I didn’t see it,” Reid said . “I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a false start].” “I thought the guys battled like crazy. We had over 100 yards in penalties. We’ve got to take care of that,” Reid added. Overall, the Chiefs were hit with 11 penalties for 105 yards throughout the game. Denver received six penalties for a total of 45 yards. Mahomes did everything he could to win the game, throwing for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers shut down the Atlanta Falcons , 16-0, at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday despite Baker Mayfield having zero completions . Mayfield went 0-of-3, as the nonstop rain forced the Buccaneers to abandon their passing game to survive the Falcons. He had four carries for 14 yards. Bucky Irving had 27 carries for 170 yards and one touchdown, while Kenny Gainwell added 25 carries for 140 yards. Chase McLaughlin kicked 3-of-3 for 10 points. item.title: Donte DiVincenzo is reportedly on track to return to the Timberwolves this season
item.description: Donte DiVincenzo is reportedly on track to return to the Timberwolves this season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There has been an uptick in ruptured Achilles tendon injuries over the past few years. Kevin Durant, Damian Lillard, Tyrese Haliburton, and Jayson Tatum have all suffered this ghastly injury. Thankfully, those players have shown that coming back strong is possible for modern-day players. Back in the day, this injury was a career-ending one, but it seems modern medicine and physical therapy have helped today's athletes properly recover. One of the players currently dealing with the injury is Minnesota Timberwolves guard Donte DiVincenzo, who is on track to return as soon as he can. Donte DiVincenzo believes he can come back this season It has been a tough road for DiVincenzo because he was having a great year for the Timberwolves in the 2025-26 season. Getting that taken away from him in the Playoffs was tough to take, but it seems that he has been doing well rehabbing his Achilles tendon. For a long time, a lot of people dreaded this injury because not only did it lead to long absences, but it also had long-term effects on athletes. Thankfully, DiVincenzo seems to have a strong team around him that is helping him heal properly enough to convince him that he will be ready to go at some point in the 2026-27 season. MORE: Donte DiVincenzo has opened up about his Achilles injury and what he felt about it Of course, most players might say that it would be best to properly step away for the entire year. Lillard and Haliburton did that this season, and they have been good ever since coming back. DiVincenzo seems intent to come back and help the Timberwolves this season. "We can easily say you’re on schedule, if not certainly ahead of schedule…When this happened, the goal was to be back for this season. That’s not even a question," DiVincenzo's doctor said about a potential return to the Timberwolves this season . Of course, the doctor did also say that the mental side of this injury is also a big part of what will happen. If DiVincenzo feels truly healthy and ready, he could come back this season, but it is also valid if he decides to take his time and return in the 2027-28 campaign. After more than 1,800 days away from the Octagon, the Irishman finally stepped back into competition for the first time since his devastating leg injury against Dustin Poirier in July 2021. Having spent years dealing with legal troubles and recovering from his injury, McGregor was finally ready to compete again. But his return could hardly have gone worse. item.description: Jayden Daniels snaps unbelievable drought with Commanders' win over Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Commanders have a long way to go to turn their season around, but Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles was a necessary step. Washington scored 27 consecutive points after falling behind 10-0 in the first quarter, extending the Eagles' losing streak to six and, somehow, sticking around in NFC East contention at 2-4-1. For Jayden Daniels, the win was especially meaningful because it was a feeling he simply hadn't experienced in a long, long time. Here's what you need to know about the wild winless streak Daniels ended on "Sunday Night Football." MORE: Andy Reid disputes game-changing false start call Jayden Daniels snaps winless drought Daniels' win on Sunday night was his first in more than a year. Before beating the Eagles, Daniels' most recent win came all the way back on Oct. 5, 2025 against the Chargers . Since then, Daniels has injured his non-throwing elbow three times and gone 0-7-1 as a starter. The Commanders have won during that stretch, including a victory over the Seahawks earlier this season, but Marcus Mariota was at the helm of the offense. For a player who put together one of the most impressive rookie seasons in NFL history and went to the NFC championship game in year one, going more than a year without a win was astounding. That drought, however, is now over, and Daniels looked like he was playing with some more freedom Sunday night as he racked up 217 yards through the air despite missing Terry McLaurin.
